transcript.text:
Excellent points from all three of you. Let me work through the implications for our submission.

First, on the voluntary disclosure question: Under our DOJ-response policy, authorization of voluntary disclosure in the initial response is required once finance has confirmed improper payments and a repayment figure. Maya has confirmed $275,000 in improper payments with controllership. However, Maya has also flagged on the record that this figure reflects the full ledger reconciliation, not a figure mapped to the four-distributor, 2019–2021 scope that Thomas confirmed. That means we have a confirmed improper payments finding, but we do not yet have a repayment figure that is reliably tied to the subpoena's actual scope. In my judgment, the policy's requirement for a confirmed 'repayment figure' means a figure we can stand behind as accurately reflecting the amounts at issue in this matter — not a broader ledger figure that may include payments outside the subpoena's scope.

So here is my proposed approach: First, we will not authorize voluntary disclosure in the initial submission until Maya completes the scope-mapped reconciliation against the four distributors for calendar years 2019 through 2021. Second, the draft response will describe our preservation efforts and investigation plan, but will not commit to a voluntary disclosure or a specific repayment amount until the scoped reconciliation is complete. Third, the interview plan in our submission will be revised to reflect that the implicated VP has retained separate counsel and will not participate without written consent from that counsel — we will not present an interview commitment we cannot execute.

Thomas, I need you to finalize your subpoena-scope memorandum as quickly as possible so Maya can use the four-distributor scope parameters to complete the scoped reconciliation. Maya, can you commit to completing that scope-mapped reconciliation on an expedited basis? Jordan, please ensure the revised interview plan language accounts for the separate-counsel constraint.

If all of that is acceptable, I will not sign the submission until the scoped repayment figure is confirmed and the interview plan is revised. Do we have agreement on this approach?
